claim: CGEL excludes subject uses of personal-pronoun expressions modified by poor or lucky. The empirical target here is the external function of the whole expression.
evidence_summary: A first-person book review has “lucky me gets to interview Jolene”. The finite predicate gets has no separate overt subject. Reading lucky me as a detached exclamation leaves the subject of gets unexplained.
finding: Record an integrated subject use in informal writing. Third-person agreement is compatible with a special construction or a nominal reanalysis of me. This undated token establishes neither the form’s distribution across registers nor its availability in 2002.
inference: Does an integrated subject use of lucky me establish how me is categorized inside it?

evidence.source: 3rdplacelibrary. Review of Knee Deep by Jolene Perry. The StoryGraph.
evidence.passage: §10.2, p. 430, discussion of poor and lucky. CGEL bars subject function and marks Poor you have got the night shift again with an asterisk. The attested subject has different agreement.
evidence.example: The writer embeds “lucky me gets to interview Jolene” in connected first-person prose. The expression occurs immediately before a finite lexical verb.
evidence.establishes: The integrated subject reading accounts for gets. Category conversion and the range of the subject use require separate evidence. Automated direct access returned 403.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraph, interview with Jolene. Indexed text, posting date unverified.
